analysis: This batch contains documentation only: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/fused-causal-prefill-attention.md lines 1-5) and one added configuration-table row in docs/architecture/inference.md (head line 671). Both describe a performance change. Full-attention prompt chunks for fused-kernel head_dims (64/72/80/96/128, and 256 on NAX from 1024 queries) use a single MLX `.causal` SDPA call instead of 128-query blocks. Sliding-window, softcap, vision-span, bidirectional, live packed paged KV and Gemma 4 paths are excluded. The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0 escape hatch is foreground-only. No executable code is supplied in this batch. The referenced implementation files are AttentionV1.swift (usesFusedCausalPrefill) and PagedLayerCache.swift (prefillAttend), and their correctness is outside the evidence. Security relevance: TB-007/T-028 cover in-process plaintext and GPU residue; the change reduces materialized score tensors and does not add persistence. T-007/T-027 cover output integrity; the docs state Qwen on M5 may differ within bf16 rounding and that Nemotron Lightning was not measured. That is numerical drift, not an adversary-controlled regression. T-041/SEC-035 cover the TTFT timing oracle; faster prefill does not change cache scoping. An adversarial consumer can influence chunk length and thus which path is chosen. That should be harmless if the masks are correct. The next review pass should confirm the following in the source: (1) usesFusedCausalPrefill correctly excludes windowed, softcapped, vision and bidirectional masks, so a consumer cannot get non-causal or cross-row attention in packed batches; (2) the .causal offset is correct when the chunk follows cached prefix KV (query offset vs key length), which matters for prefix-cache adoption correctness; (3) memory admission and activation bounds are not lowered on the basis of the reduced peak; (4) the new DARKBLOOM_* env key is handled by DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification, which rejects unrecognized performance-affecting keys. No regression was identified from the docs.
